Chemical Industry Sites in Vietnam Resume Operations After Dengue Outbreak Contained

HO CHI MINH CITY, Vietnam, June 14 – Operations at several chemical production facilities in southern Vietnam have resumed after a dengue fever outbreak among workers was declared contained this week, industry representatives said.

The outbreak, first identified in late May at three sites in Binh Duong and Long An provinces, affected more than 80 employees across multiple shifts, according to the Vietnam Chemicals Trade Association. Production at affected plants, including those operated by Hoa Binh Chemicals and Mekong Industrial Solutions, was curtailed for nearly two weeks as health authorities quarantined exposed workers and conducted disinfection campaigns.

“Thanks to rapid cooperation between factory management and local health officials, all infected workers received timely treatment, and there have been no fatalities,” said Nguyen Van Minh, deputy director at Hoa Binh Chemicals. He added that daily temperature screenings and mosquito control measures are now in place.

Dengue fever, a mosquito-borne viral disease, is endemic in Vietnam’s southern provinces. This year, the rainy season arrived earlier than usual, contributing to a spike in mosquito populations near industrial sites, according to health officials.

Analysts estimate the outbreak reduced output at affected facilities by as much as 35% during the shutdown. “The disruption was significant, especially for clients waiting on deliveries of industrial solvents and specialty chemicals,” said Le Thi Thu Trang, an analyst at Saigon Industry Review.

All impacted operations have now resumed, with the Vietnam Chemicals Trade Association reporting that staffing levels and production have returned to normal as of June 13.
